claim: PC networks with local rules converge to backprop gradients on arbitrary graphs, so the learning rule is not a barrier in principle.
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM scaffold; background only.

claim: In practice PC matches backprop only to about 5-7 layers; ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 falls from 92.83 (BP) to 43.19 (PC-CE) or 70.44 (best iPC); Tiny ImageNet 9.52 vs 58.00.
agent_test: None for the scaffold; warns against importing PC training.

claim: Depth failure is caused by badly balanced layer energies (about 1e-6 ratio first vs last layer at state rate 0.01) and exponential signal decay; ePC and muPC fix much of it (ePC ResNet-18 92.17 vs BP 92.36).
agent_test: None; engineering result.

claim: Plain PC is unstable and slow in language models: Gaussian PC transformer perplexity 590.08 vs BP 162.64, categorical (KL) PC 175.90; iPC masked-LM 106.19 vs BP 120.02 with 10/10 seeds converging.
agent_test: None; small-scale models only.

claim: PC training costs about 100x backprop compute for the CNN case because of iterative inference; claimed speed advantages are not consistently observed.
agent_test: Compare any iterative refine-until-settled operator against one-pass at equal tokens.

claim: Expectation suppression (expected stimuli give smaller responses) is replicated in many studies but is also explained by neural adaptation and attention, so it does not uniquely support prediction error. Post-2021 review (Feuerriegel 2021) finds genuine suppression mainly after weeks of learning; Richter and de Lange 2019 (N=34) found it vanishes when stimuli are unattended.
agent_test: None; neuroscience background.

claim: Laminar and cell-type evidence partly fits the process theory (7T deep-layer illusory-figure activation; mouse V1 error-like and prediction-like neurons) but alternative models fit equally or better.
agent_test: None.

claim: Evidence for error propagation across contiguous hierarchical levels is scarce; most PP-like dynamics come from simple stimuli.
agent_test: Check whether multi-level critique steps in a scaffold add anything over one-level critique at equal tokens.

claim: PredNet (forward only errors, top-down predictions) beats a matched activation-forwarding CNN-LSTM on next-frame prediction (rotating faces MSE 0.0152 vs 0.0180; SSIM 0.937 vs 0.907) and supports a linear steering readout (74% variance at 1K labels).
agent_test: Scaffold analogue: pass only the delta between draft and critique upward, versus the full draft, at equal tokens.

claim: GPT-2 activations plus forecasts of words up to 8 words ahead improve fMRI brain scores by 23% (+-9%); frontoparietal cortex forecasts farther and more semantically than temporal cortex (304 participants).
agent_test: Background only; one group's result (the four lines are one study).

claim: The brain-LLM fit may reflect general feature transfer rather than prediction: encoding performance correlates r=0.847 with next-word prediction and r=0.864 with general transfer (97 representations), not significantly different.
agent_test: None.

claim: Language prediction signals are hierarchical (syntax, phonemes, semantics dissociable; N400 tracks BERT/GPT-2 surprisal) but cross-lingual and layer-wise checks do not always reproduce prediction-specific effects.
agent_test: None.

claim: Expectation did not change sensory representation fidelity under 75% valid cues in one EEG study (BF10 about 0.16), contrary to sharpening accounts. Kok 2012 sharpening has no close independent replication found; Rideaux 2026 (preprint) favours dampening.
agent_test: None.

claim: Next-token training is argued to be only partly predictive coding; LLMs lack action-coupled generative models and hierarchical compositional structure.
agent_test: None; position papers, no data.

claim: PC-motivated signals (surprise against context priors) as features raise hallucination-detector AUROC from 0.8274 (base) to 0.8669 on a 200-item HaluBench subset; naive averaging of signals gave 0.48. Full text re-read: n=200 is the only evaluation, no CIs, Lynx comparison mixes AUROC with accuracy.
agent_test: Replicate the surprise-vs-context signal as a verify step on a larger set at equal tokens; N=200 is small.

claim: A PC-style correction block did not improve language-model loss in a 158M hybrid ablation (12.630 full vs 12.413 without it).
agent_test: None; single preprint, base-loss only.

claim: Look-ahead foresight resampling (Predictive-Decoding, MPC style, not PC by name) gains 7.2% on GSM8K and 25.3% on AlfWorld at about 50% of MCTS FLOPs; 76.5% of GSM8K errors occur when generation is myopic. Also helps on code (Llama-3 HumanEval pass@1 57.3 vs 44.3 plain vs 53.5 beam at 290e12 FLOPs) and PDDL (38.3 vs 35.0); gain over equal-budget self-consistency about 0.4 points in the one readable GSM8K row.
agent_test: Direct candidate: foresight reweighting as a step operator vs best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: Prospective configuration (settle neuron activity before weight change) reduces interference and learns faster at small batch in PC networks.
agent_test: None.

claim: PC-native memory (DeltaNet-PC) reaches 100% recall up to length = dim = 1,024, and temporal PC with RTRL matches BPTT (1.865 vs 1.864 BPC).
agent_test: Background; different mechanisms, each one paper.

claim: Self-correction by the model alone, with no outside signal, does not beat plain voting at equal calls: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 -> 74.7 after two self-correct rounds; debate below self-consistency at 9 responses; self-repair at equal budget gives 0.97x to 1.05x of plain sampling.
agent_test: Any predict-compare-update operator must be compared with self-consistency at equal calls and with an external check signal.

claim: No study isolates passing only the residual (draft vs critic delta) against full re-reading at equal tokens. Closest evidence says feedback quality, not format, decides repair gains (human feedback 33.3% -> 52.6% repair success).
agent_test: Run it: delta-only vs full-reread revision at matched tokens, same verifier, N above 200, CI reported.

claim: PC training scale evidence ends at 128-layer residual networks on simple classification (muPC); no result shows PC language models beyond small transformers.
agent_test: None; irrelevant to a prompt scaffold.

claim: Hierarchical language prediction (syntactic category, phonemes, semantics dissociable; word level informs phoneme level) is shown in EEG N=19 and MEG N=3; no test separating syntax, semantics and discourse was found.
agent_test: None; background.

claim: Attention gates expectation suppression: in one fMRI study (N=34) the expectation x attention interaction was significant in V1 (F=7.706), LOC (F=12.580) and TOFC (F=16.955), so suppression alone cannot separate error coding from attention.
agent_test: None; neuroscience background.
